longest_story.synopsis: Big Jack Bancroft kidnaps Kay Kyser and his saxophonist (whom he resembles) in order to get on Kyser's radio show, "The College of Musical Knowledge" in order to hide from the Police. Kyser has to find a way to tip off Batman to this and invite him to his program in order to round up the crook.
longest_story.notes: Per Sprang in interview with Craig Delich, the splash page was re-arranged by DC's art department, not him, to almost replicate the cover.
longest_story.keywords: Batcave; Batmobile; belt radio; Gotham City; Gotham City University

longest_story.title: Robin, the Boy Failure!
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Commissioner James Gordon; Penguin [Oswald Cobblepot] (villain, cameo); The Crime Surgeon [Steve Travers] (villain, cameo); The Yellow Masks (villains, introduc tion for all)
longest_story.synopsis: Dick Grayson suffers from a case of amnesia after rescuing a woman from near death. Bruce devises a plan for the youngster to "assume" the role of Robin in order to try and shock him into remembering his true identity.
longest_story.notes: Inker credit verified by Craig Delich; we previously credited Dick Sprang and before that suggested Gene McDonald.
longest_story.keywords: Batcave; Batmobile; Batplane; Gotham City; Wayne Mansion

longest_story.title: Three's a Crime!
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Numbers [Carl C. Cave] (villain); Jack Fasset (villain, a fence); Pete (villain)
longest_story.synopsis: Carl Cave is lucky with numbers, especially concerning the lucky number "3", and he believes that number can protect him from the minions of the law...and Batman himself!
longest_story.notes: Penciler credit verified by Sprang. Inker credit verified by Craig Delich; we previously suggested Gene McDonald.
longest_story.keywords: Batcave; Batmobile; Gotham City; Gotham Gazette; Gotham Sun; Gotham World

longest_story.synopsis: A new villain decides to create a criminal empire underwater, so the Dynamic Duo create their own weapon of offense: the Sub-Batmarine!

longest_story.title: The Experiment of Professor Zero
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Commissioner James Gordon; Mr. Carlyle (banker); Mr. Gresham (financier); Mr. Parnell (automobile magnate); Professor Zero (villain, introduction, death); Beefy (villain, death)
longest_story.synopsis: Batman and Robin fall victim, like others, to a mad scientist who has found a way to reduce humans to pigmy size!
longest_story.notes:
Inker credit verified by Craig Delich; we previously suggested Howard Sherman or Gene McDonald.

Oddity: On page 2, panel 3, Batman titles this case "The Pigmy Plot" in his personal casebook on page 1, but "The Experiment of Professor Zero" on the last page.
longest_story.keywords: Bat-Signal; Batcave; Gotham City

longest_story.title: The Sound-Effect Crimes!
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; The Joker (villain); Joker's gang (villains)
longest_story.synopsis: The sound effects from a radio drama spur the Joker to institute a new crime idea: that of using sound to create panic among the city's populace in order to make easy scores.
longest_story.notes: Penciler credit verified by Sprang. Inker credit verified by Craig Delich; we previously suggested Howard Sherman and Gene McDonald.

longest_story.title: The Ghost of Gotham City!
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Commissioner James Gordon; Judge Whipple; District Attorney Robert J. Pierce; Judge Whipple; Dr. Paul Visio [as Rifle Rafferty] (villain, introduction); Lefty (villain)
longest_story.synopsis: A clever doctor uses a phony "ghost" of executed mobster Rifle Rafferty and a group of stool pigeons within Gotham City's mobs in order to convince the Police and the Dynamic Duo that Rafferty has come back from the dead to exact revenge.
longest_story.keywords: Bat-Signal; Batcave; Batmobile; Gotham City; Gotham News
